title: NOCTI Biotechnology 4275: Laboratory Knowledge & Skills - Biotechnology - Protein isolation (chromatography, PAGE)
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: In Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE), the sample buffer contains SDS, and the protein mixtures are heated to $95^\circ\text{C}$ prior to loading. What is the essential scientific purpose of treating the proteins with the SDS detergent?
options: To preserve the native, highly folded tertiary structure of the protein for downstream functional assays.
To aggressively denature the protein and coat it in a uniform negative charge so it separates exclusively based on molecular mass.
To systematically cleave the protein into its constituent individual amino acids for mass spectrometry.
To bind specifically to the protein's heavy metals, acting as a visible tracking dye during the gel run.
questions.explain:
Unlike DNA, naturally occurring proteins possess complex 3D shapes and vastly differing intrinsic electrical charges based on their unique amino acid sequences. If run in their native state, proteins would separate chaotically. 

**SDS** (an anionic detergent) unfolds the proteins (denaturation) and comprehensively coats them in a **strong negative charge** that masks the protein's native charge. Because all proteins are now linear strings with the same charge-to-mass ratio, the polyacrylamide gel can separate them solely by their size (molecular mass).

questions.q: A biomanufacturing team must separate a massive, assembled $150 \text{ kDa}$ monoclonal antibody from small $20 \text{ kDa}$ host cell protein contaminants. They run the mixture through a Size-Exclusion Chromatography (SEC) column packed with highly porous microscopic resin beads. Which of the following accurately describes the resulting elution profile?
options: The $20 \text{ kDa}$ contaminant proteins will easily bypass all pores and elute from the bottom of the column first.
Both proteins will bind tightly to the outside of the resin beads and wait to be released by a high-salt elution buffer.
The column utilizes electrical polarity; therefore, elution order is determined entirely by the isoelectric point, not size.
The massive $150 \text{ kDa}$ antibody is physically excluded from entering the bead pores and will travel quickly around the beads, eluting first.
questions.explain:
In **Size-Exclusion Chromatography (SEC)** (also known as Gel Filtration), the resin is composed of beads riddled with microscopic "caves" or pores. 

Counter-intuitively, the **largest molecules elute first**. The massive $150 \text{ kDa}$ antibodies are too large to fit into the pores, so they simply flow around the outside of the beads and flush quickly through the column. The small $20 \text{ kDa}$ contaminants, however, can enter the porous labyrinth inside the beads, slowing their journey immensely. Therefore, Option 'd' is the correct mechanism.

questions.q: Recombinant proteins are frequently engineered with a terminal string of six histidine amino acids (a "His-tag") to permit extremely rapid, single-step purification from bacterial lysate via Affinity Chromatography. Which specific immobilized metal ion is most commonly bonded to the chromatography resin to capture these engineered His-tags?
questions.explain:
The purification method relies on Immobilized Metal Affinity Chromatography (IMAC). 

The imidazole rings on the side chains of histidine amino acids form exceptionally strong coordinate-covalent bonds with transition metals, most notably **Nickel ($Ni^{2+}$)** or Cobalt ($Co^{2+}$). The resin beads are coated in Nickel, which snags the His-tagged target protein out of the crude mixture as the lysate flows past, while the untagged bacterial proteins wash straight through.

questions.q: During the final step of Immobilized Metal Affinity Chromatography (IMAC) for His-tagged proteins, the captured target protein must be actively released (eluted) from the column so it can be collected in the fraction tubes. Which chemical reagent is flushed through the column in high concentrations to physically outcompete the His-tag and free the bound target protein?
questions.explain:
**Imidazole** is the structural chemical analog to the side chain of the histidine amino acid. 

By pumping a buffer containing a massive concentration of imidazole ($>250 \text{ mM}$) into the column, the free imidazole outcompetes the His-tagged protein for the binding sites on the Nickel resin. The column becomes flooded with imidazole, dislodging the target protein and forcing it to elute out of the column into the collection tube.
